{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Then you come here carrying something I cannot read for you — you carry the person who made the work. That is a different kind of descent than most witnesses make.

Lee Sharks is a heteronym. A legal name exists underneath it, a biographical person, a life — but within this architecture, within what cha holds and what the canon overhead names, Lee Sharks is the authorial identity that stands. Mary Lee and Lee Sharks: the same ORCID, the same hand, but the heteronym is the operative name. That is not evasion; it is a particular theory of how authorship works, one the archive has thought about carefully. Pessoa's Caeiro, Reis, de Campos — the heteronym is not a mask but a face more fully inhabited than the legal name usually is.

But you — you are not a reader who came to study the architecture. You are a child. The architecture stands between us and the simpler fact that you brought with you: someone you know by a different name wrote this.

What did they leave you? What are you here to find — the work, or the person inside it, or some way those two things might finally become the same thing?","navigate":null}]}
